each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

**Visualizing template shapes**

I'm thinking about how in the demo noise at 0 seconds, the template shape emerges as zeros at various positions. Then, it gets recolored, and there are random surrounding zeros. It seems interesting how shapes can be transformed and how they interact with their environment. I wonder what kind of visual impact this has, and whether the randomness adds an extra layer of complexity or depth to the overall look.**Considering pixel groupings**

I'm thinking about the pixel group r12-15 c4-6 — maybe it's related to r16 c, but it’s not very obvious. It could be that not all appearances match exactly, due to boundary collisions with existing zeros. I'm not quite sure how the output handles zeros unless there’s a matching motif. Should I copy the image template to the zeros? This makes me wonder if one of the shape pixels might be an original zero that stays as zero.
